gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much preamp gain the USB/XLR hybrids need in XLR mode. The Samson Q9U's -57 dBV/Pa works out to 1.41 mV/Pa, only 2 dB hotter than a Shure SM7B. If the SM7B needs more than 60 dB of gain, the Q9U still needs about 58 dB of clean gain from the interface you add later.
standout_why: I compared against itechguides.com (rank 8). It gives sensitivity and gain needed only for the XLR-only SM7B: '-59 dBV/Pa' and 'more than 60 dB of preamp gain'. It gives no sensitivity figure for the MV7+ or the PodMic USB. Both MusicRadar pages ChatGPT cited loaded only their titles in my fetches, so I couldn't check them. ChatGPT's answer sells 'the ability to upgrade to an audio interface later' but never says how much gain that upgrade needs.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. The Q9U and PodMic USB come out about the same in XLR mode (both -57 dB, about 1.4 mV/Pa). Either way, a shopper who wants the XLR upgrade needs an interface with about 58 dB of clean gain or an inline booster. I couldn't source the MV7+ XLR sensitivity, so I can't rank it on this figure. The page should add a 'gain needed via XLR' column next to 'Outputs'.

findings.label: XLR sensitivity
findings.note: Maker spec. The same page lists 50 Hz to 20 kHz, 250 Ω and 2.13 lb (0.97 kg). It shows 'Coming Soon / Preorder Today' with no price.

findings.label: Preamp gain needed via XLR, compared with an SM7B
findings.value: about 58 dB (2 dB less than an SM7B)
findings.source_title: Best Microphone: MV7+, PodMic USB, MV6, NT1, SM7B Compared (itechguides)
findings.note: itechguides gives the SM7B as '-59 dBV/Pa' needing 'more than 60 dB of preamp gain'. (-57) - (-59) = 2 dB hotter, so 60 - 2 = about 58 dB for the same recording level. The SM7B baseline comes from this rival page, not from Shure.

findings.label: Sensitivity
findings.source_title: Rode PodMic USB Review / Test (Podcastage, Bandrew Scott)
findings.note: Named reviewer. The page gives '-57dB' without a reference unit and dates the review 'Jul 25' with no year. Taking it as dBV/Pa: 1000 × 10^(-57/20) = 1.41 mV/Pa, which is the same as the Q9U and needs about 58 dB of gain (60 - 2) by the itechguides SM7B baseline. Podcastage's own test settings were 'Computer Level: 51dB' plus '+8dB' boosted in post, or 59 dB in total.

findings.label: SM7B baseline (the gain reference for XLR dynamic mics)
findings.value: -59 dBV/Pa; needs more than 60 dB of preamp gain
findings.source_title: Best Microphone: MV7+, PodMic USB, MV6, NT1, SM7B Compared (itechguides)
findings.note: This is a rival page in ChatGPT's results. It also says a booster is 'not guaranteed' to be needed with every interface.
